executive_summary: USD/CHF closed at 0.82432 on 2026-10-30 (best available, flagged: the latest Federal Reserve noon rate is 0.8248 for 23 October) [17] and EUR/CHF at 0.92064, the SNB's focus pair, after a month in which the franc gained 0.81% against the dollar and 1.46% against the euro while losing ground over longer windows (USD/CHF +1.91% over 3M, +5.59% over 6M and +3.33% over 1Y, each a weaker franc). October's move was a safe-haven rotation driven by French fiscal and political stress, with the OAT-Bund spread at 152.5bp on 20 October after a high near 159bp, the widest since 2011 and EUR/CHF fixing at 0.9211 on 22 October from 0.9478 on 30 September [18][19]. Against that, the SNB policy rate sits at 0%, the lowest in G10+SGD and 387.5bp below the Fed midpoint, 250bp below the ECB deposit rate and 460bp below the RBA, and only about 6bp of SNB tightening was priced for December in mid-October while the Fed, ECB, BoE and BoJ all have hikes priced or delivered [15][29][31]. Valuation is mixed: the BIS real effective rate fell to 98.37 in September, its lowest of 33 monthly readings since January 2024 and 4.60 points lower over a year, yet World Bank PPP factors still put the franc 12.9% expensive against the dollar and 42.4% against the euro [36][37]. The tension is that the macro and external factors favour the franc - Swiss CPI rose to 1.0% in September, the SNB dropped its 'increased willingness' to intervene, the Q2 current account surplus was CHF 23.7bn, and Switzerland is AAA with gross debt near 38% of GDP while France's 10-year yield approached its highest since 2002 - but the carry penalty is large and widening, [1][2][24][27], and CME Swiss franc futures, observed 2026-10-28, already discount about 4.5% a year of franc appreciation against the dollar [40]. Leveraged funds are the most short CHF in the 25 weeks since May (net -17,502 contracts) while asset managers are the least short (net -25,067), a split that leaves room for a short squeeze if European stress escalates [35]. We are Neutral tactically (weighted score +0.03, conviction 2) because carry and US rate momentum offset the haven bid ahead of the 3 November Swiss CPI, and mildly Bullish strategically (+0.13, conviction 2) on the external surplus, fiscal strength and a 2027 SNB hike option, with the caveat that our 6M USD/CHF target of 0.8050 is only 6 pips through the forward, so the view earns spot direction but not carry.

valuation.trade_weighted_assessment: The SNB estimated a roughly 3% trade-weighted depreciation from June to September 2026, in line with wider rate differentials, and October's 1.46% gain against the euro has only partly reversed it; the BIS real rate at 98.37 sits 3.2 points below its 33-month mean [2][36].
valuation.what_is_priced_in: The real effective rate prices a franc that has already absorbed most of the 2026 widening in rate differentials: a 387.5bp gap to the Fed and 250bp to the ECB with SNB hikes deferred into 2027. The 12.9% premium to PPP against the dollar is a structural feature of the franc - it has held a premium for decades on the back of a 5-10% of GDP current account surplus - rather than a mispricing that mean-reverts inside six months.
valuation.actionability: Structural rather than actionable: the REER low argues against chasing franc weakness, but PPP deviations of 10-80% against every peer have no record of closing on a 1-6 month horizon. PPP figures use World Bank conversion factors that are the latest published, best available, flagged, and should be read as orders of magnitude.

tactical.analysis: The SNB policy rate at 0% is the lowest of the ten G10+SGD rate-setters, 125bp below the BoJ, 175bp below the Riksbank, 250bp below the ECB and the Bank of Canada, 375bp below the BoE, 387.5bp below the Fed midpoint and 460bp below the RBA [1][29][31][32]. Every one of those peers except Norges Bank either hiked in the past two months or has a hike priced for the next eight weeks, so the negative differential is widening in real time: the BoE is expected to move on 5 November, the Riksbank on 4 November, and the Fed, ECB and BoJ each carry live December hikes [15][31][32]. The SNB, by contrast, held on 24 September with a conditional forecast that keeps inflation within 0-2% at a 0% rate through 2028, and mid-October pricing showed only about 6bp of SNB tightening by December [1][15]. Front-end yields confirm the market's verdict: the Swiss 2Y eased to 0.18% on 30 October from 0.263% at the 30 September close (best available, flagged: a second daily series showed 0.235% on 29 October, so the end-October level carries a 5bp source range), so the US-Swiss 2Y gap stands at 443bp against the US 2Y at 4.61% [21]. The 10Y at 0.47% is 446bp below Treasuries and 285bp below Bunds (Bund 3.325% on Trading Economics; a second daily series put the Bund at 3.40%, an 8bp source divergence, so the spread is best available, flagged at 285-293bp), and the 2s10s curve at +29bp signals a long hold rather than a tightening cycle [22][34]. CME Swiss franc futures, observed 2026-10-28, roll USD/CHF at a 454.8bp annualised discount [40], so a franc long pays roughly 4.5% a year to hold against the dollar before any spot move. Our assessment is that the December SNB meeting is a hold with 85% probability, which is close to market pricing; the tactical mispricing is not at the SNB but in peer hikes, where we see the Fed December hike at 55% rather than the fully priced level reported in mid-October [15]. On a 2-4 week horizon the carry channel dominates and is franc-negative, but the gap is already well known, which keeps confidence at 58.

strategic.analysis: Over six months the policy gap is set to widen before it narrows: if the Fed, ECB, BoE and BoJ each deliver one 25bp hike by March 2027 while the SNB holds on 10 December, the franc's average carry deficit against the four widens from 283bp to 308bp [15][29][31][32]. The offset is an SNB hike option in 2027: Bloomberg Economics sees the policy rate at 0.25% by end-2027 with a possible first move in March 2027 in a high-oil scenario, while LSEG pricing in late September implied at least 0.75% by September 2027 and UBS flagged that the weaker franc could bring its June 2027 call forward [15]. Those two sources disagree by 50bp on the 12-month path, and the fall in the 2Y from 0.263% on 30 September to 0.18% on 30 October shows the more hawkish pricing has decayed [21]. The September conditional forecast rises from 0.7% in 2026 to 0.8% in 2027 and 2028, all inside the 0-2% band, which does not require tightening; the board also said hardly any second-round effects are visible [1][2]. A March 2027 hike therefore needs core inflation to move from 0.5% toward 1% and the franc to stay weak, and we put that at 30%. Even with one SNB hike in March, the differential to the Fed would be 387.5bp or wider and to the ECB 250-275bp, so carry stays heavily against the franc through the horizon. The SNB also pays 0.25pp less on sight deposits above the threshold, a tiering that keeps money-market rates slightly below the policy rate [1]. Rates remain franc-negative strategically, but the asymmetry is shifting: the next policy surprise in Switzerland is more likely to be hawkish than dovish, which caps confidence at 53.

tactical.analysis: Swiss headline CPI rose to 1.0% in September from 0.8% in August, the fastest since September 2024 and in line with consensus, while FSO core CPI edged up to 0.5% from 0.4% [4]. The drivers are cost-push and energy-led: transport inflation is 3.6% and housing and energy 2.2%, while food (-1.0%), clothing (-1.9%) and household goods (-0.3%) are still deflating, so goods prices rather than domestic services are moving the headline [4]. The SNB's TM15 trimmed mean was 0.6% in August (best available, flagged: the August figure as reported in the SNB's summary of deliberations, with no September update located) and the board saw hardly any second-round effects [2]. Growth is strong but uneven: SECO's sport-adjusted Q2 GDP rose 1.5% q/q, the strongest since Q3 2021, but chemicals and pharmaceuticals contributed most of it (+10.5%) and private consumption grew only 0.3% [5]. Leading indicators are softening from high levels: the KOF barometer fell to 107.6 in October from 109.1, below the 108.3 consensus, and the procure.ch PMI dropped to 55.3 in September from 57.1 with purchase prices at 70 [7][8]. The labour market is soft: registered unemployment is 3.1% seasonally adjusted for a fifth month and FSO's first estimate of 2026 nominal wage growth is just 0.4% [9][10]. The 3 November October CPI is the tactical swing event: a print at 1.2% or higher would revive December hike pricing and support the franc, while 0.8% or lower would confirm the SNB's on-hold path. With headline rising and growth momentum easing in equal measure, the factor is Neutral at 53.

strategic.analysis: Over six months the inflation trajectory is upward from the lowest base in G10+SGD: the SNB's conditional forecast has inflation rising further in Q4 2026 before easing through 2027, with averages of 0.7% in 2026 and 0.8% in 2027 and 2028 [1]. That forecast was built on a 0% policy rate and already includes the effect of the weaker franc, which the SNB said lifts the medium-term path [1][2]. Brent near USD 117-123 in late October is above the levels behind the September forecast, so headline risk into early 2027 is skewed toward 1.2-1.5% [19]. Growth outperformance is real but fading: SECO raised its 2026 sport-adjusted forecast to 1.7% from 0.9% and holds 1.6% for 2027, yet expects a countertrend in the second half after the pharma-driven Q2 [6]. Wage pressure remains muted, with firms expecting only +1.2% nominal by July 2027 and the KOF projecting real wage growth of 0.7% [11]. Relative to peers Switzerland has the lowest inflation (1.0% against 3.7% in the US and 3.8% in the euro area) and the highest real policy rate gap in reverse, but rising Swiss inflation is the only route by which the SNB narrows the carry deficit [4]. We therefore read inflation and growth as mildly franc-supportive strategically: they raise the probability of an SNB hike in March or June 2027 from near zero to roughly 30-40% without threatening price stability. Confidence is held to 50 because the pharma-driven growth figures are volatile and the KOF and PMI have both turned lower.

tactical.analysis: The global risk regime is transitioning from complacent to stressed in one region: the VIX rose to 17.2 on 29 October from 16.04 a month earlier, US high-yield spreads widened 18bp to 326bp, and US investment-grade spreads remain tight at 89bp. The stress is European and sovereign: the French 10Y reached about 4.96% on 20 October, near an early-October peak of 4.9937% that was the highest since July 2002, and the OAT-Bund spread was reported at 152.5bp after a high near 159bp, the widest since 2011 [18]. That level exceeds the 150bp threshold that ING flagged for a further EUR/CHF leg lower [19]. The franc's safe-haven behaviour has returned: it gained more than 2% against the euro in October, the strongest monthly rise since late 2023, and the EUR/CHF reference rate fell to 0.9211 on 22 October [18][19]. Equity risk appetite has not cracked - the SMI closed at 14,810.66 on 30 October, up 8.72% in a month and 21.06% over a year - so the haven bid is targeted at euro sovereign risk rather than a broad risk-off [23]. The franc's implied beta is visible in the cross: EUR/CHF fell 1.46% in October while USD/CHF fell only 0.81% and GBP/CHF rose 0.69%, the pattern of a euro-specific haven flow. Tail scenarios that would extend the bid are a French government collapse, a renewed Hormuz disruption pushing Brent above USD 130, or a US equity correction from record levels; we put the combined probability of at least one over four weeks at 30%. With European stress active and equities still firm, the factor is Bullish for the franc at 53.

Rate guidance is neutral: the conditional forecast at a 0% rate keeps inflation inside 0-2%, and the decision was taken by Schlegel, Martin and Tschudin without any signalled bias [2]. The SNB's communication style is low-frequency and surprise-prone - UBS economists noted that the SNB has a history of surprising markets - and there is no scheduled communication between now and the 10 December assessment beyond occasional speeches. Markets broadly buy the guidance, with about 6bp of hikes priced for December, so the gap between guidance and pricing is near zero [15]. The intervention retreat tilts the factor Bullish at 52 tactically.

strategic.analysis: Over six months the dollar-liquidity picture is two-sided. The Fed is likely to deliver one more hike, with markets pricing about 75bp of tightening through end-2027 and the dot plot showing one more 2026 move, which keeps the dollar on the right side of the smile [15]. But balance-sheet shrinkage has slowed to a crawl at about USD 2bn a week, and reserves near USD 2.96tn are far from scarce, so a liquidity-driven dollar squeeze of the 2019 or 2022 kind is unlikely [30]. If US growth slows into 2027 and the Fed signals an end to hikes - Bloomberg Economics expects a 25bp cut in the second half of 2027 - the dollar would move toward the bottom of the smile, where the franc usually gains against the dollar [15]. Swiss institutions are structural dollar borrowers to fund foreign assets, so any widening of the dollar basis would be franc-negative first and franc-positive later as carry unwinds. The SNB's substantial dollar holdings within CHF 770bn of reserves are not being reallocated in size. These forces balance over the strategic horizon. The factor is Neutral at 48.

tactical.rationale: At tactical weights the policy factor dominates, and a 387.5bp dollar carry and 250bp euro carry against a 0% SNB rate deliver the single largest contribution of -0.139 [1][29][31]. Dollar funding conditions add -0.055 because SOFR at 3.94%, negligible swap-line use and a hiking Fed keep franc-funded carry comfortable [30]. Against those, the European sovereign shock - an OAT-Bund spread of 152.5bp and a French 10Y near its highest since 2002 - restored the franc's haven role in October, and the risk, positioning, event and fiscal factors together contribute +0.156 [18][19]. External balance and the SNB's retreat from an increased willingness to intervene add a further +0.069 [2][24]. The interaction that matters is between carry and haven: carry is reinforced by peer hikes on 4-5 November and in December, while the haven bid is reinforced by the leveraged-fund short of -17,502 contracts, the widest in the 25-week sample, that would cover into any further stress [35]. The net +0.0316 says those forces cancel at a 2-4 week horizon. What is priced is a contained French problem and an SNB on hold; our edge is that the market underprices a further spread widening (30% odds) but also overprices the speed at which the franc can keep rallying against a 4.5% annualised forward discount. The path of least resistance is a 0.8150-0.8300 range in USD/CHF and 0.9100-0.9300 in EUR/CHF. The key dated catalysts are Swiss October CPI on 3 November, the Riksbank on 4 November, the BoE and Norges Bank on 5 November, US CPI on 10 November and the SNB on 10 December. Actionability is limited for spot: a Neutral call is best expressed through cheap franc optionality, with one-month USD/CHF implied vol at 6.82% on CME-listed options observed 2026-10-28 and the 35th percentile of its recent range [40]. A Swiss CPI print at 1.3% or higher, or an OAT-Bund spread above 170bp, would move the tactical view to Bullish.

strategic.rationale: At strategic weights the policy factor still carries the most weight at 0.24, and its -0.127 contribution reflects a carry deficit that widens from about 283bp to 308bp against the four largest peers by March 2027 [15]. External balance at a 0.16 weight is the offset: a CHF 23.7bn Q2 current account surplus, 9.2% of GDP, and a real effective rate at a 33-month low of 98.37 contribute +0.104 [24][36]. Guidance at a 0.12 weight adds +0.066 as the SNB has abandoned its increased willingness to intervene and its December forecast is likely to edge 2027 inflation higher [1][2]. Inflation dynamics add +0.050 because rising Swiss inflation from 1.0% is the route to a 2027 SNB hike [4], and fiscal quality adds +0.041 as AAA Switzerland contrasts with France's widest spread since 2011 [18][28]. The factors interact: the external surplus and fiscal quality are slow but persistent, while the carry drag is large but has a visible end as peer hiking cycles mature in H1 2027. The net +0.133 implies a mildly stronger franc over 1-6 months. What is priced matters most here: CME Swiss franc futures, observed 2026-10-28, already discount 4.5% a year of franc appreciation against the dollar and about 3.0% against the euro [40], so the six-month USD/CHF forward of 0.8056 sits only 6 pips above our 0.8050 base case. Our edge is therefore in direction and in the tails, not in the base case: we see a 25% chance of USD/CHF at 0.7800 that the forward does not price. The path of least resistance is a gradual franc grind against the dollar as US rate momentum peaks, with EUR/CHF anchored at 0.90-0.92 by the SNB. Key catalysts are the SNB on 10 December and 18 March 2027, the FOMC on 9 December, the ECB on 17 December and the BoJ on 18 December. Conviction is 2 because the score clears the Neutral band by only 0.033 and the highest-weight factor points the other way. Actionability is best through six-month franc calls or put spreads on USD/CHF and EUR/CHF, since spot longs pay carry that consumes most of the base-case move.

consensus_divergence.why_we_differ: Consensus forecasts were set before October's French spread shock and treat the franc purely as a funding currency. We weight the SNB's retreat from increased intervention willingness, which removes the floor under EUR/CHF that bank forecasts implicitly assume. We also weight the external surplus at a cheap real exchange rate, which carry-driven forecasts underweight. Finally, Swiss inflation at 1.0% and rising gives the SNB a reason to follow peers in 2027 that the curve does not price.

factors_changed.reason: The OAT-Bund spread rose from 111.2bp to 152.5bp and the franc regained its haven role, gaining more than 2% against the euro in October.
The Q2 current account surplus of CHF 23.7bn and a REER at a 33-month low turned the near-term external signal positive.
The 22 October summary confirmed the board no longer sees an increased willingness to intervene as necessary, removing the intervention cap.
French fiscal stress made relative sovereign quality an active franc driver rather than background.
CPI rose to 1.0% in September, opening a 2027 SNB hike option.
EUR/CHF broke below its 200d average and the 0.93225 support, offsetting the USD/CHF uptrend.
Fed balance-sheet run-off slowed to about USD 2bn a week and the end of the hiking phase is within six months.

seasonality.pattern: Year-end dollar funding demand and portfolio rebalancing in late November and December, with thin liquidity in the last two weeks of December; the franc has tended to firm in January as year-end carry positions are cut.
seasonality.historical_magnitude: Not quantified from a published study; the effect is typically a few tenths of a percent and is swamped by policy events such as the 10 December SNB meeting.
seasonality.current_alignment: Mildly supportive of the dollar into December (consistent with the tactical Bearish F10 reading) and mildly franc-positive in early January (consistent with the strategic grind lower in USD/CHF).

assumptions: Spot levels (30 October closes, best available, flagged against the Federal Reserve noon rate of 0.8248 for 23 October), moving averages, realised volatilities, 52-week ranges and support/resistance zones are from weekday closing bars to 2026-10-30; realised volatility is annualised on 252 trading days and carry ratios are stated as carry over 60-day realised volatility.

Forward points are derived from the annualised roll between listed CME Swiss franc futures contracts observed 2026-10-28 (best available, flagged, as single-day readings) (USD/CHF -454.8bp, EUR/CHF -295.7bp); they include the rate differential and any cross-currency basis, which cannot be separated without an OIS curve.

USD/CHF implied volatility and risk reversals are CME-listed option quotes observed 2026-10-28; EUR/CHF implied vol is an estimate from the two dollar legs and their realised correlation, not a quote, and is used only for context. The implied-vol percentile uses 49 observations since 2026-08-21 because no one-year implied-vol history is freely available.

Probabilities attached to central-bank decisions in the rate table and catalysts are the dossier's own estimates unless described as market pricing. Policy rates are the latest published decisions: SNB 0% (24 September), Fed 3.75-4.00% midpoint 3.875% (28 October), ECB deposit 2.50% (29 October), BoJ 1.25% (30 October), BoC 2.50% (28 October hike), RBNZ 2.75% (28 October; the 4-3 vote split is best available, flagged), BoE 3.75%, RBA 4.60%, Norges Bank 4.50%, Riksbank 1.75%; Singapore runs an exchange-rate band and has no policy rate.

SNB market pricing conflicts across sources: about 6bp of December hikes in mid-October (Bloomberg) versus roughly even December odds in late September (LSEG via a secondary report); the later figure is used, consistent with the 2Y yield falling from 0.263% on 30 September to 0.18% on 30 October.

The OAT-Bund spread is stated at 152.5bp (20 October), after a high near 159bp; higher readings on other daily measures in the week of 22 October are not used because they could not be matched to a published source.
CFTC percentiles are measured over the 25 weekly reports from 12 May to 27 October 2026, not a multi-year history.

PPP deviations use World Bank GDP PPP conversion factors, the latest published; they are best available, flagged, because the values were not re-displayed at the cited page on 2026-10-31, and should be read as orders of magnitude.

Three-month EUR/USD, JPY/USD and CHF/USD cross-currency basis, a SARON OIS strip, sovereign CDS and the SNB nominal effective index are not available from free sources; these are stated as gaps where relevant.
Overall confidence is the weight-averaged factor confidence for each horizon; scenario probabilities are fixed at 50/25/25.
Peer CPI and core figures in the macro table are the latest national releases as of 2026-10-31; Swiss unemployment is SECO's registered rate (3.1%) with the ILO-basis 5.0% noted for comparability.
